conventions.convention: The metric has signature (-,+,+,+); the frame is a smooth future unit timelike observer field u, with g(u,u)=-1, and Δ projects onto its pointwise rest space. A frame is distinct from a chart or tetrad.
Coordinates use x⁰=ct. Geometric entropy divergence has units J K⁻¹ m⁻⁴; multiplication by c gives entropy production per physical volume per second. Q has units Pa, and cQ is physical energy flux.
The gradient branch uses nonnegative C1 coefficients and closures Π=-ζcθ, π=-2ηcσ, Q=-(κ/c)ΔY, and V=-LΔZ, where Y=dT+Ta and Z=d(μ/T). Future timelikeness of J is separately required: g(V,V)<n².

The bulk branch has positive C1 ζ and τ, β=τ/ζ, entropy current S=(s-βΠ²/(2T))u, and the derivative-corrected relaxation law βDΠ+Π/(ζc)=-θ-(TΠ/2)div(βu/T). Its application declares an open near-equilibrium regime around constant zero-gradient reference data with Π=0.

The state function and state map are C2. The gradient theorem additionally requires smooth dissipative fields; the bulk branch requires smooth Π. Balances and entropy divergence are pointwise classical expressions.

The homogeneous witness uses t=x⁰/c on O=(-cδ,∞)×R³, δ>0 seconds, constant state and coefficients, u=∂x⁰, and Π(t)=Π₀ exp(-t/τ₀). Its amplitude is chosen so the full field and first-derivative data remain in the declared regime.
Countable Choice AC_ω is carried through the geometric supplier chain; no stronger choice principle is asserted.

load_bearing.statement: Adopt source-free number and stress balances, S=su+Q/T-μV/T, and Π=-ζcθ, π=-2ηcσ, Q=-(κ/c)ΔY, V=-LΔZ, with nonnegative C1 coefficients and the separately imposed future-timelike number-current condition.

For the selected bulk-only branch, adopt source-free stress and particle balances, S=(s-βΠ²/(2T))u, and βDΠ+Π/(ζc)=-θ-(TΠ/2)div(βu/T), where β=τ/ζ and ζ,τ>0 are C1, within the declared near-equilibrium regime.

An actual solution of the selected bulk balances and corrected law, with the stated regularity, positivity and regime hypotheses, satisfies div S=Π²/(ζcT)≥0. Under the additional reference-data condition, the stated constant-state Minkowski fields with Π(t)=Π₀ exp(-t/τ₀) give a homogeneous solution for sufficiently small amplitude.
For an actual sufficiently regular solution of the selected gradient branch in its declared regime, div S=(ζcθ²+2ηc σ^{ab}σ_{ab})/T+κΔ^{ab}Y_aY_b/(cT²)+LΔ^{ab}Z_aZ_b≥0.

concerns.concern: Step 1.1 says the solution satisfies 'every input in [F2]' and that 'the given solution is smooth'. The Statement and Given specify only C2 state function/map, smooth u and Π, and C1 coefficients. The cited lem-tgr-bulk-relaxation-entropy states its result for 'smooth ... local state' and 'every actual smooth solution'; F2 here repeats that stronger wording. The identity remains obtainable at the consumer's regularity by the same first-derivative Gibbs/product-rule calculation, but the proof does not explicitly supply that extension or reconcile the smoothness wording.

alerts.finding: The item declares 'status: published', but its complete verification block contains only 'precheck: pass', with no audited, verified or repair record. SCHEMA.md requires publication evidence beyond a format pass for a published proved item. Its rest-space positivity and projection proof checked out; this finding concerns publication metadata.

seams_checked.note: The used material postulate, state definitions, x⁰=ct units and local entropy criterion are preserved. The entropy criterion is identified after the sign calculation rather than used as its mathematical proof.

The bulk stress, corrected law, extended current, signs, units and homogeneous witness match lem-tgr-bulk-relaxation-entropy. The assertion that its smooth-solution hypotheses are exactly met by the consumer's C2/C1 data needs the regularity clarification recorded in concerns.

The linearized-material postulate uses the bulk branch as formulation context and separately stipulates the constant-coefficient adiabatic first-variation system. It does not infer nonlinear existence or causality from positive relaxation time or the entropy identity.

The supported heat postulate adopts the heat closure with Q=q/c and κ=A₀/N, sets the other transport coefficients to zero, declares its regime and future-timelike number current, and explicitly replaces source-free stress balance by a supported balance with u·f=0.
